story: Lakshmana, Rama's younger brother, left his wife and his comforts to follow Rama into the forest for 14 years. He guarded Rama and Sita day and night, and in the war in Lanka he killed Ravana's son Indrajit.
belief: He is remembered as the ideal brother and as an incarnation of Shesha, the serpent on which Vishnu rests. His loyalty is held up as the model of seva, service to the one you love.
turns: In anger he cut off the nose of Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, which helped set off Ravana's revenge. He also left Sita alone when she insisted he go after Rama, and that is when Ravana took her.
facts: Legend says he did not sleep for the 14 years so he could keep watch.
His wife Urmila is said to have slept for those 14 years in his place.
The 'Lakshmana rekha' is named after him.
